svg.title: Jumpstart LocalBox: nested Azure Local learning lab topology
svg.desc: One outer Azure virtual machine contains two nested Azure Local nodes, shared cluster storage, a management environment, a small AKS cluster, and an Ubuntu VM that can be live-migrated. Azure Arc provides a control path, not a general VPN.
svg.text: The learning lab: two nodes, one physical fault boundary
Topology illustration based on the recorded lab, not a Microsoft reference architecture or portal screenshot.
Azure control plane
Azure portal / ARM / Azure Arc / resource identities
Your management computer
Private Arc SSH and cluster-connect tunnels
Outer Azure VM: LocalBox-Client / Hyper-V
Bastion opens this Windows management desktop. Both Azure Local servers below are nested VMs.
AzLHOST1
Azure Local node / Hyper-V
Initial Ubuntu owner for the exercise
Source-node console: VM Connect
AzLHOST2
Azure Local node / Hyper-V
Destination for a planned live migration
No permanent cluster master
AzLMGMT environment
Domain controller / DNS
Lab router / VLAN gateways
Management, not a third cluster node
Storage Spaces Direct / Cluster Shared Volumes
The final VM configuration and disks remain on cluster storage during a same-cluster move.
Azure Arc resource bridge
Custom location / VM and AKS operators
AKS on Azure Local + NGINX
One Linux worker + one required control plane, separate from the two Azure Local nodes.
Ubuntu VM + web observer
Guest identity stays separate from the externally observed cluster Owner Node.
Important: stopping the outer LocalBox VM removes both simulated nodes and management services.
A physical production deployment uses independent servers and its own validated network, storage, security and availability design.
